adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:145 — ANCHOR_PATTERN strips any tag starting with "a" (e.g. <a href="javascript:..." onclick=...>, <audio onerror=...>) with arbitrary attributes, and English files are compared against themselves, so the English source files never get their anchor/a-prefixed tags checked and translations copying them pass silently

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, `englishFile` resolves to the same file when verifying an `_en.properties` file, so `value` and `englishValue` are identical. `santizeAnchors()` then removes any tags matching `ANCHOR_PATTERN` (`</?a[^>]*>`) from `value` whenever they match the English tag, meaning English source strings’ `<a ...>` (and also tags like `<audio ...>` since the regex matches any tag starting with `a`) are effectively exempt from the later OWASP sanitizer check. As a result, unsafe/undesired anchor (or `a*`) tags in English can pass silently, and translations that copy them exactly will also pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:126 — For linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*/error-invalid-multivalued-size, any {N,choice,...} segment (without a closing brace) is replaced with "..." before sanitizing, so HTML such as injected inside the choice pattern passes unchecked

adjudication.rationale: In normalizeValue(), for keys starting with linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit or equal to error-invalid-multivalued-size, the code does `value = value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...");` before sanitizing/comparing. This removes the entire `{N,choice,...}` segment from `value`, so any HTML embedded inside that choice expression (e.g., ``) would be stripped out during normalization and therefore never reach the sanitizer/diff check, letting illegal HTML in the original properties file escape detection. The finding’s claim about matching choice segments *without* a closing `}` is incorrect (the regex requires `}`), but the bypass for closed choice patterns is still real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:157 — The "Didn't find anchor tag" message leaves out the key and file name, so on a real run with hundreds of files you cannot tell which translation broke

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:111 — The common prefix and suffix scans can overlap (e.g. value "aa" vs sanitized "a"), so sanitized.substring(start, len-end) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the problem

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the diff introduces prefix/suffix trimming to highlight differences: it computes `start` as the common prefix length, then `end` as the common suffix length, and then calls `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)`. These scans can overlap when one string is shorter but shares the same prefix and suffix (e.g., value="aa", sanitized="a" -> start=1, end=1 => sanitized.length()-end=0, so `sanitized.substring(1,0)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException). The code has no guard to prevent `start > (length - end)` before taking substrings, so the verifier can crash instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:74 — English reference file is derived by regex rewriting the absolute path (resources-community->resources, _xx->_en), silently coupling the verifier to repo directory layout and file naming.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:88 — Anchor attributes are only compared to the English string, never validated themselves, so `<a href="javascript:...">` or `onclick` in an English source key passes and is then allowed verbatim in every translation.

adjudication.rationale: In `verifySafeHtml()`, anchors are handled by `santizeAnchors()`, which only checks that each ``/`` tag in the translated value exactly equals the corresponding tag in the English source (`Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`), and then removes it from `value` before OWASP sanitization. Because anchors are removed prior to sanitization and there is no validation of anchor attributes (e.g., `href="javascript:..."`, `onclick=...`) in either the English string or the translation, a dangerous `` present in the English source would pass the verifier and translations could include the same dangerous tag and also pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:126 — For linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* and error-invalid-multivalued-size keys, the whole `{n,choice,...}` block is dropped before sanitizing, so arbitrary HTML inside a choice (e.g. `{0,choice,0#}`) is not checked.

adjudication.rationale: In `normalizeValue`, for keys matching `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` or `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, the code does `value = value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...");`, which removes the entire `{n,choice,...}` segment before `policy.sanitize(value)` runs. As a result, any HTML embedded inside a choice block would be stripped from `value` and never compared against the sanitized output, so the verifier would fail to report illegal HTML placed inside `{...,choice,...}` for those keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:33 — Assertions weakened from contains to hasItem with only a substring match, so unexpected extra messages (e.g. spurious Illegal HTML) pass silently

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.verifyDuplicateKeysDetected(), the assertion was changed from `Matchers.contains(Matchers.containsString(...))` (which enforces the list contents/order, effectively failing if extra messages are present) to `Matchers.hasItem(Matchers.containsString(...))`, which only checks at least one matching message exists. This can let unexpected additional verifier messages (e.g., from the newly added `verifySafeHtml()` in VerifyMessageProperties) pass without failing the test, weakening test strictness and potentially masking regressions.
